nl.statement:
A two-sample semi-supervised discrete causal experiment. A known covariate alphabet \([d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}\) with \(d\ge2\), binary treatment \(A\in\{0,1\}\) and binary outcome \(Y\in\{0,1\}\) give the complete record space \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\). A law \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}([d]\times\{0,1\}^2)\) determines cell masses \(p_x=P(X=x)\), propensities \(e_x=P(A=1\mid X=x)\) on occupied cells, outcome regressions \(\mu_{ax}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\), treatment--covariate cell masses \(s_{ax}=P(X=x,A=a)\), outcome-marked masses \(q_{ax}=s_{ax}\mu_{ax}\), and the target \(\tau(P)=\sum_{x=1}^d p_x(\mu_{1x}-\mu_{0x})\in[-1,1]\). For a known overlap constant \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the unrestricted class \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) collects the laws with \(\epsilon\le e_x\le1-\epsilon\) on every occupied cell; no minimum cell mass is imposed and null cells are permitted. The observation experiment \(\mathcal E_{n,m,d,\epsilon}\) supplies \(n\ge1\) complete labeled records \(\mathcal L_n\sim P^{\otimes n}\) together with \(m\ge0\) outcome-unlabeled records \(\mathcal U_m\sim P_{XA}^{\otimes m}\) from the same population, the two samples being independent, so that outcome-bearing information has size \(n\) while treatment--covariate information has size \(N=n+m\). Estimators \(\mathcal T_{n,m,d}\) are the measurable real functions of \((\mathcal L_n,\mathcal U_m)\); the minimax risk is \(R_\epsilon(n,m,d)=\inf_{T\in\mathcal T_{n,m,d}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E[(T-\tau(P))^2]\), compared with the explicit annotation-frontier rate \(r_\epsilon(n,m,d)=\min\{1,n^{-1}+d^2/(N^2\log^2(en))\}\) and attained by the mixed-information hybrid \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}\). Asymptotic statements run along arbitrary sequences \((m_n)_{n\ge1}\) and \((d_n)_{n\ge1}\); the two-sided constants \(c_\epsilon,C_\epsilon\in(0,\infty)\) depend only on \(\epsilon\). Lower bounds are indexed by fuzzy hypotheses \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) on \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) whose full random table \(P_{XA}\) has identical distribution, together with the finite illustrative pair \(\Pi_0^{\mathrm{small}},\Pi_1^{\mathrm{small}}\) and the finite calculation \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{small}}\) at \(d=2\), \(\epsilon=1/4\). — Encoding: `abbrev Obs (d : Nat) := Fin d x Bool x Bool`, `abbrev AuxObs (d : Nat) := Fin d x Bool`, `structure DiscreteLaw (d : Nat) where pmf : PMF (Obs d)`, `Sample n m d := (Fin n -> Obs d) x (Fin m -> AuxObs d)`, with `jointMass`, `cellMass`, `armMass`, `propensity`, `outcomeMean`, `markedMass`, `auxMarginal : DiscreteLaw d -> PMF (AuxObs d)`, `labeledProductLaw`, `auxProductLaw`, `annotationLaw = (labeledProductLaw P n).prod (auxProductLaw P m)`. All in Basic.lean, namespace `CausalSmith.Stat.SemisupervisedDiscreteAteAnnotationFrontier`.
Substrate survey (bypass-justified, define-local): searched `../doc/API.md` sections `10z Reusable minimax and nonparametric reduction substrate`, `8h PO/`, `18 Experimentation/` and the cluster roots `Causalean/Stat/`, `Causalean/Estimation/`, `Causalean/Estimation/Efficiency/`, `Causalean/Estimation/MinimaxATE/`, `Causalean/PO/` for a two-sample labeled/unlabeled finite-alphabet discrete-ATE world; concept words grepped: `semisupervised`, `unlabeled`, `two-sample`, `annotation`, `auxiliary sample`, `discrete ATE`, `overlap cone`. Causalean carries the general measure-theoretic PO/ATE machinery and the experiment-level minimax tools but no finite-alphabet two-sample discrete-ATE world; every sibling Stat run (`CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_DiscreteAteMinimaxLoggap_Research/Basic.lean`, `CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_DiscreteAteHeterogeneityFrontier_Research/Basic.lean`) owns its own finite model layer over `Causalean.Stat.Sample` + Mathlib `PMF`, and `doc/API.md` `Workspace context` fixes the dependency direction `CausalSmith -> Causalean` only (no cross-run imports). BYPASS-JUSTIFIED: abstraction mismatch (measure-theoretic vs finite algebraic) plus the one-way package rule.
Analogous module F2 should mirror line-for-line: `CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_DiscreteAteMinimaxLoggap_Research/Basic.lean` (`DiscreteLaw`, `Obs`, `cellMass`, `propensity`, `outcomeMean`, `Overlap`, `ateFunctional`, `mse`, `worstCaseMSE`, `minimaxRisk`) - the one-sample (m = 0) version of this exact world; the gap to bridge is the second, outcome-free sample and the `n` vs `n+m` information split.

A finite potential-outcome overlay on the same discrete world. A full-data law on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^4\) carries the record \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) with binary potential outcomes \(Y(a)\in\{0,1\}\); consistency requires \(Y=Y(A)\) almost surely and conditional exchangeability requires \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp\!\!\!\perp A\mid X\). Together with occupied-cell overlap these identify the causal contrast \(E[Y(1)-Y(0)]\) as the observed-data functional \(\tau(P)\) of the induced observed marginal. — Encoding: `abbrev FullObs (d) := Fin d x Bool x Bool x Bool x Bool`, `structure PotentialLaw (d) where pmf : PMF (FullObs d)`, `fullMass`, `poAtom`, `observedMarginal : PotentialLaw d -> DiscreteLaw d`; `Consistency` and `ConditionalExchangeability` are finite-sum Props on `PotentialLaw`.
Search trace: grepped `Causalean/PO/` and `../doc/API.md` section `8h PO/` for `Consistency`, `conditional exchangeability`, `ignorability`, `PODataFrame`, `POSystem` (Causalean does carry `PO` systems, `Backdoor`, `POManskiIVSystem`); Mathlib-side check `lean_leansearch "conditional independence of potential outcomes given covariates"` returns only generic `ProbabilityTheory.CondIndep`. BYPASS-JUSTIFIED: the Causalean PO analogue is a measure-theoretic PO system with abstract outcome spaces, whereas this note needs a purely finite `PMF` overlay used only to certify identification of `tau` once; the sibling `STAT_DiscreteAteMinimaxLoggap_Research/Basic.lean` (`PotentialLaw`, `Consistency`, `ConditionalExchangeability`, `observedMarginal`) is the exact analogous encoding to copy.

The known-treatment--covariate-marginal benchmark experiment. An estimator observes \(n\ge1\) complete labeled records \(\mathcal L_n\sim P^{\otimes n}\) together with the exact \(2d\)-cell table \(P_{XA}\) supplied as deterministic side information, so that the decision class \(\mathcal T^{\mathrm{known}}_{n,d}\) consists of the measurable functions of \((\mathcal L_n,P_{XA})\) and the benchmark risk is \(R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)=\inf_{T\in\mathcal T^{\mathrm{known}}_{n,d}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E_{P^{\otimes n}}[(T(\mathcal L_n,P_{XA})-\tau(P))^2]\). This is the \(m\to\infty\) limit of the annotation experiment: all treatment--covariate information is revealed and no outcome information is added. — Encoding: `AuxTable d := AuxObs d -> Real` (the exact 2d-cell table), `knownSample n d := (Fin n -> Obs d) x AuxTable d`, `knownMarginalExperiment`, `knownMarginalRisk` in Basic.lean.

For a finite alphabet size \(d\) and an observed-data law \(P\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), define the average treatment effect functional by
\[
\tau(P):=\sum_{x=1}^{d}p_x(P)\bigl(\mu_{1x}(P)-\mu_{0x}(P)\bigr).
\]
Here \(p_x(P)\) is the covariate cell mass at \(x\), and \(\mu_{ax}(P)\) is the binary outcome regression in treatment arm \(a\) and covariate cell \(x\), totalized by division in the arm cell.

Define the annotation experiment by
\[
\mathcal E_{n,m,d,\epsilon}
:=
\Bigl\{
P^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m}:
P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon},\ n\ge1,\ m\ge0,\ d\ge2
\Bigr\}.
\]
The product law corresponds to \(n\) independent complete outcome-labeled records and \(m\) independent additional outcome-unlabeled treatment-covariate records, with independence between the two samples.

Lean takes the infimum over measurable real-valued estimators and supremum over precisely the bundled model class of the canonical-product expected squared error about τ(P).

nl.statement:
Put \(A_\star=7056\) and \(c^\circ=1/256\).  Let \(j_\epsilon\) be the least integer \(j\ge1\) for which \(2^{-j}\le\epsilon\), and put \(\bar\epsilon=2^{-j_\epsilon}\); thus \(0<\bar\epsilon\le\epsilon<2\bar\epsilon\).  Define \(H_\epsilon\) to be the least positive integer \(H\) satisfying the finite list
\[
 H\ge4,\qquad \frac H4\ge15+\frac{24}{c^\circ},\qquad
 Hc^\circ\bar\epsilon\ge672,
 \qquad Hc^\circ\bar\epsilon\ge24.                                      \tag{C1}
\]
The set in this minimum is nonempty because \(c^\circ\bar\epsilon>0\), and all of its tests involve integers and dyadic rationals.

For given \(n,m\), partition the labeled indices, in their original order, into blocks of sizes
\[
 M_0=\lfloor n/3\rfloor,\qquad
 n_p=\left\lfloor\frac{n-M_0}{2}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad n_f=n-M_0-n_p,
\]
and partition the auxiliary indices into blocks of sizes
\(m_p=\lfloor m/2\rfloor\) and \(m_f=m-m_p\).  The outcome block is the first labeled block; the pilot and factorial pools have sizes
\[
 M_p=n_p+m_p,\qquad M_f=n_f+m_f,\qquad
 u=M_0/8,\quad t_p=M_p/8,\quad t=M_f/8.                            \tag{C2}
\]
If \(n<24\), declare the calibration predicate \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) false.  If \(n\ge24\), put \(N=n+m\), \(\ell=\log(en)\), \(h_n=1+\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\),
\[
 L=\max\{2,\lfloor c^\circ h_n\rfloor\},\qquad
 B=\frac{H_\epsilon L}{\min(t_p,t)},\qquad
 k_0=\lfloor t_pB/4\rfloor,                                          \tag{C3}
\]
and let \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) be the conjunction of the following finite tests:
\[
 \frac1{32}\le\frac un\le\frac1{24},\qquad
 \frac1{32}\le\frac{t_p}{N},\frac tN\le\frac3{32},\qquad
 \frac13\le\frac t{t_p}\le3,\qquad L\ge\frac{c^\circ h_n}{2},   \tag{C4}
\]
\[
 t_pB\ge8,\qquad tB\ge L,\qquad
 L^4A_\star^{2L}\le n,\qquad L^6A_\star^{2L}\le n,               \tag{C5}
\]
\[
 \frac{t_pB}{4}\ge15L+12h_n,\qquad
 \left(1+\bar\epsilon\frac t{t_p}\right)^{k_0}\ge n^{12},
 \qquad \bar\epsilon tB\ge12h_n.                                  \tag{C6}
\]
These comparisons are a finite decidable computation from \((n,m,\epsilon)\): \(h_n\) is the binary length of \(n\), \(\bar\epsilon\) is dyadic, and every remaining quantity and comparison is rational.

If \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) is false, set \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}=0\).  If it is true, independently average over prefix lengths \(D_0\sim\operatorname{Poi}(u)\), \(D_p\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t_p)\), and \(D_f\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t)\), returning zero whenever a prefix exceeds its pool.  For a valid prefix, let \(J_x\) be the pilot count and call \(x\) light when \(J_x\le k_0\).  Define, with polynomial continuation at zero,
\[
 H_L(z)=\frac{1-T_L(1-2z)}{2L^2},\qquad
 E_L(z)=\frac{H_L(z)}z,\qquad G_L(z)=\frac{1-E_L(z)}z,
\]
and expand
\[
 W_{a,L}(s_0,s_1)=\frac{s_0+s_1}{B}G_L(s_a/B)
 =\sum_{r_0,r_1}c_{a,r_0,r_1}s_0^{r_0}s_1^{r_1}.
\]
For factorial-pool counts \(K_{ax}\), outcome-block success counts \(S_{ax}\), and falling factorials \((k)_r\), put
\[
 \widehat W_{a,L,x}=\sum_{r_0,r_1}c_{a,r_0,r_1}
 \frac{(K_{0x})_{r_0}(K_{1x})_{r_1}}{t^{r_0+r_1}},
 \qquad
 \widehat W^H_{a,x}=\frac{K_{0x}+K_{1x}+1}{K_{ax}+1},
\]
\[
 Z_x=\mathbf1\{J_x\le k_0\}
 \left(\frac{S_{1x}}u\widehat W_{1,L,x}-\frac{S_{0x}}u\widehat W_{0,L,x}\right)
 +\mathbf1\{J_x>k_0\}
 \left(\frac{S_{1x}}u\widehat W^H_{1,x}-\frac{S_{0x}}u\widehat W^H_{0,x}\right).
\]
The valid-prefix output is \(\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}(\sum_xZ_x)\).  Finally \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}\) is the conditional expectation of this output over the three prefix lengths given \((\mathcal L_n,\mathcal U_m)\).  It is a finite weighted sum of rationally generated polynomial coefficients, observed counts, and computable Poisson weights, and hence is a total computable measurable map.

For \(n,m,d\in\mathbb N\) and a real overlap constant \(\epsilon\), define
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}: \mathcal T_{n,m,d}
\]
as the following map from
\[
\bigl([d]\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\bigr)^n
\times
\bigl([d]\times\{0,1\}\bigr)^m
\]
to \(\mathbb R\). Put
\[
M_0=\lfloor n/3\rfloor,\qquad
n_p=\left\lfloor\frac{n-M_0}{2}\right\rfloor,\qquad
n_f=n-M_0-n_p,
\]
\[
m_p=\lfloor m/2\rfloor,\qquad
m_f=m-m_p,\qquad
M_p=n_p+m_p,\qquad
M_f=n_f+m_f,
\]
and
\[
u=\frac{M_0}{8},\qquad
t_p=\frac{M_p}{8},\qquad
t=\frac{M_f}{8}.
\]
Let \(b_n\) denote the binary-length calibration quantity used here, and set
\[
L=L(n),\qquad B=B(n,m,\epsilon),\qquad k_0=k_0(n,m,\epsilon),
\]
with \(\bar\epsilon=\bar\epsilon(\epsilon)\), \(A_\star=7056\), and \(c^\circ=1/256\). The calibration predicate \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) holds exactly when all of the following finite inequalities hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(24\le n\).
\item \textbf{(Block proportions.)}
\[
\frac1{32}\le\frac un\le\frac1{24},\qquad
\frac1{32}\le\frac{t_p}{n+m}\le\frac3{32},\qquad
\frac1{32}\le\frac t{n+m}\le\frac3{32},\qquad
\frac13\le\frac t{t_p}\le3.
\]
\item \textbf{(Degree and scale.)}
\[
\frac{c^\circ b_n}{2}\le L,\qquad
8\le t_pB,\qquad
L\le tB.
\]
\item \textbf{(Polynomial size.)}
\[
L^4A_\star^{2L}\le n,\qquad
L^6A_\star^{2L}\le n.
\]
\item \textbf{(Tail calibration.)}
\[
15L+12b_n\le\frac{t_pB}{4},\qquad
n^{12}\le\left(1+\bar\epsilon\frac t{t_p}\right)^{k_0},\qquad
12b_n\le\bar\epsilon tB.
\]
\end{itemize}
If \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) fails, set
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}(\mathcal L_n,\mathcal U_m)=0.
\]
If \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) holds, set
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}(\mathcal L_n,\mathcal U_m)
=
\sum_{r_0=0}^{M_0}
\sum_{r_p=0}^{M_p}
\sum_{r_f=0}^{M_f}
\Pr\{\operatorname{Poi}(u)=r_0\}
\Pr\{\operatorname{Poi}(t_p)=r_p\}
\Pr\{\operatorname{Poi}(t)=r_f\}
\,\Phi_\epsilon(\mathcal L_n,\mathcal U_m;r_0,r_p,r_f),
\]
where
\[
\Phi_\epsilon(\mathcal L_n,\mathcal U_m;r_0,r_p,r_f)
=
\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}\left(\sum_{x\in[d]} Z_x\right).
\]
For each \(x\in[d]\), let \(J_x\) be the pilot-prefix count in cell \(x\), let \(S_{ax}\) be the outcome-block prefix count with covariate \(x\), treatment \(a\), and outcome \(1\), and let \(K_{ax}\) be the factorial-pool prefix count with covariate \(x\) and treatment \(a\). Then
\[
Z_x
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{S_{1x}}u\,\widehat W_{1,L,x}
-
\dfrac{S_{0x}}u\,\widehat W_{0,L,x},
& J_x\le k_0,\\[1.2em]
\dfrac{S_{1x}}u\,\dfrac{K_{0x}+K_{1x}+1}{K_{1x}+1}
-
\dfrac{S_{0x}}u\,\dfrac{K_{0x}+K_{1x}+1}{K_{0x}+1},
& k_0<J_x.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(\widehat W_{a,L,x}\) is the factorial lift, at degree \(L\), scale \(B\), and intensity \(t\), of the light-cell polynomial weight
\[
W_{a,L}(s_0,s_1)=\frac{s_0+s_1}{B}G_L(s_a/B),
\]
where
\[
H_L(z)=\frac{1-T_L(1-2z)}{2L^2},\qquad
E_L(z)=\frac{H_L(z)}z,\qquad
G_L(z)=\frac{1-E_L(z)}z,
\]
with polynomial continuation at zero.

review.note: The dyadic calibration, ordered block splits, finite calibration tests, truncated independent Poisson-prefix average, light/heavy statistic, factorial polynomial lift, and clipping agree extensionally with the paper construction.

nl.statement:
Let \(N=n+m\) and \(\ell_n=\log(en)\).  In the regime \(\min\{1,d^2/(N^2\ell_n^2)\}\le C_\epsilon/n\), let \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) be point masses at the two laws concentrated on \(X=1\), with \(e_1=1/2\), \(\mu_{01}=0\), and \(\mu_{11}=1/2\mp h_n\), where \(h_n=c_\epsilon/\sqrt n\le1/4\).  In the complementary regime use the following approximation-dual construction.  Put \(L=\lceil C_\epsilon^\circ\ell_n\rceil\), \(B=b_\epsilon L/N\), \(a=\gamma_\epsilon B/L^2\), and \(\kappa=(1-2\epsilon)/\epsilon\), with the constants calibrated in \(\mathrm{lem:common\mbox{-}marginal\mbox{-}poisson\mbox{-}prior}\).  On \(I=[a/\kappa,B]\), let \(\sigma\) be the finite signed measure of total variation one furnished by \texttt{lem:finite-alternation-duality}, which annihilates \(1,p,\ldots,p^L\) and satisfies \(\int p/(p+a)\,d\sigma(p)\ge c_\epsilon>0\).  Write \(h=d\sigma/d|\sigma|\), and define
\[
 \nu(dp)=\frac{a}{p+a}|\sigma|(dp)\quad(p\in I),
 \qquad
 \nu(\{0\})=1-\int_I\frac{a}{p+a}|\sigma|(dp).
\]
Choose \(k=\min\{d-1,\lfloor c_\epsilon^\circ NL\rfloor\}\) rare cells.  Draw their raw masses independently from \(\nu\), put \(s_i=\epsilon(p_i+a)\) when \(p_i>0\), and set \(e_i=s_i/p_i\).  The reservoir raw mass is \(p_*=1-kE_\nu[p]\), with propensity \(1/2\) and zero outcomes.  Divide every raw cell mass by \(S=p_*+\sum_{i=1}^kp_i\).  Under \(\Pi_1\), put \(\mu_{1i}=(1+h(p_i))/2\); under \(\Pi_0\), put \(\mu_{1i}=(1-h(p_i))/2\); under both put \(\mu_{0i}=0\), and assign identical legal values at raw mass zero.  Remaining alphabet cells have mass zero.  In either branch \(\Pi_0\) and \(\Pi_1\) are probability measures on \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) and induce exactly the same random \(P_{XA}\).

\[
C_\epsilon,\quad C_\epsilon^\circ,\quad b_0,\quad b_\epsilon,\quad
\gamma_\epsilon,\quad c_\epsilon^\circ,\quad c_\epsilon,\quad C_d
\]
with all eight constants positive and \(c_\epsilon\le 1/4\).  A common-marginal prior handle at \((n,m,d)\) consists of integers \(L,k\), real numbers \(B,a\), and a calibrated recipe supplying two induced priors, denoted \(\Pi_0(H)\) and \(\Pi_1(H)\), on laws on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), subject to
\[
L=\left\lceil C_\epsilon^\circ \log(en)\right\rceil,\qquad
B=\frac{b_0L}{n+m},\qquad
a=\frac{\gamma_\epsilon B}{L^2},
\]
and
\[
k=\min\left\{d-1,\left\lfloor c_\epsilon^\circ(n+m)L\right\rfloor\right\}.
\]

\[

 \frac{S_{0x}}u\frac{K_{0x}+K_{1x}+1}{K_{0x}+1}\right\}.
\]
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\),
\[
 |E_PZ^H-\tau(P)|\le C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/t\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P(Z^H)\le C_\epsilon(u^{-1}+t^{-1}).
\]

\[
S_{ax}\sim \operatorname{Poi}(u q_{ax}),
\qquad
K_{ax}\sim \operatorname{Poi}(t s_{ax}),
\qquad a\in\{0,1\},\ x\in[d],
\]

\sum_{x=1}^d
\left\{

-
\frac{S_{0x}}{u}\frac{K_{0x}+K_{1x}+1}{K_{0x}+1}
\right\}.
\]
Writing \(\tau(P)\) for the average treatment effect functional in \cref{obj:def:ate-functional},
\[
\left|E_P Z^H-\tau(P)\right|
\le
C\min\{1,d/t\},
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_P(Z^H)
\le
C\left(u^{-1}+t^{-1}\right).
\]

Let \(\Theta\) be a nonempty parameter set, let \(\mathcal Z\) and \(\mathcal C\) be nonempty finite sets, and let \(\beta_-\le\beta_+\) be real numbers. \[

\]

\[

\]
where \(\psi\) ranges over all maps \(\mathcal Z\times\mathbb R^{\mathcal C}\to[\beta_-,\beta_+]\) whose section \(w\mapsto\psi(z,w)\) is Borel measurable for each \(z\in\mathcal Z\). Then \(\widetilde{\mathfrak R}_\star\le\mathfrak R_m\) for every \(m\ge0\).
